one_liner: Artificial Societies builds a foundation model to simulate human behavior for decision-making. YC participation warrants a look, but the company has already raised seed funding.

top_signals.signal: Listed in Y Combinator’s recent European cohort.
Kindred Capital led the March 2025 pre-seed round, and Point72 Ventures led the May 2025 seed round.

Model score 76.7 of 100 (at the top of the reference cohort). Three recorded founders, a co-founder CTO, and flags for YC participation, deep tech, business customers, and university background lifted the score. The technical-founder flag also lifted it but is not confirmed by the founder records.

team: James He (CEO) attended the University of Cambridge; Patrick Sharpe (CPO) previously worked at iptiQ; Tom Whittle is listed as co-founder and CTO.
why_early: Whether either round was priced is unknown. The reported pre-seed and seed rounds put the company past HTGF’s first-round outreach window.
devils_advocate_risks: It is unknown how well the simulations predict real-world behavior.
Using anonymized social media or transaction data could raise privacy and regulatory concerns.
next_step: If the HTGF Industrial Tech team follows up despite the prior rounds, ask: How have you tested the model’s predictions against observed human behavior?
